items.topic: Integration test location, build-tag, and runner wiring
items.context: The scenario has mock-based unit tests under api/livedesktop/*_test.go, no integration tests, and no build-tag convention in the repo. We need a home for real-backend tests and a way for 'vrooli scenario test vrooli-emulator' to pick them up while still allowing developers to run unit-only tests quickly. Location choice also determines whether tests can reach unexported internals (same-package) vs only the public HTTP surface (external package).

options.label: New file api/livedesktop/integration_test.go with '//go:build integration' tag; add integration.enabled=true to .vrooli/testing.json so 'vrooli scenario test' runs 'go test -tags=integration ./...'
options.rationale: Same-package access lets tests reach Service internals (e.g. verify janitor state, sessions map) when needed. Build tag keeps default 'go test ./...' fast for unit-only runs. Minimal new infrastructure — one file, one tag, one testing.json edit.

options.label: New package api/integrationtest/ with regular _test.go files (no build tag); list it under testing.json's unit.languages.go with a separate 'integration' bucket; add a Makefile target 'make test-integration'
options.rationale: Cleanest separation — integration concerns live in their own directory. Downside: tests can only use the public HTTP surface, which is fine for most assertions but loses the option to peek at unexported state. Also adds a new top-level api/ sibling folder.

options.label: Top-level api/integration_test.go in package main, gated by env var (e.g. EMULATOR_INTEGRATION=1) instead of a build tag
options.rationale: Env-var gating is more familiar than build tags to some teams and is easier to flip in CI. Downside: package main can't access livedesktop internals cleanly, and env-var gating is less greppable than build tags.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: How integration tests exercise the real LinuxBackend
items.context: The current api/main.go wires Service + Handler + LinuxBackend + janitor onto a gorilla/mux router. Integration tests can either reconstruct that wiring in-process and front it with httptest.Server, or compile/spawn the actual 'vrooli-emulator-api' binary as a subprocess and drive it via HTTP. In-process is faster and has richer failure diagnostics; subprocess is closer to operator reality and catches wiring bugs that only surface at process startup.

options.label: In-process: construct LinuxBackend + Service + Handler in test setup; front with httptest.Server; drive via net/http client
options.rationale: Fast (no build step per test run), easy teardown, tests can use Service directly for invariant checks. LinuxBackend still uses real Xvfb/x11vnc/websockify, so the OS-level integration signal is preserved. Matches the existing 'setupTestDB(t)' style precedent used in other Vrooli scenarios.

options.label: Subprocess: 'go build' the API binary into t.TempDir(), exec it on a random port, wait for /health, drive via HTTP; kill on cleanup
options.rationale: Closest to operator reality — catches main.go wiring regressions, environment-variable handling, and startup-time bugs. Downside: every test run pays a Go build cost (~5-10s), port coordination adds complexity, and debugging a failed subprocess is harder.

options.label: Hybrid: most tests in-process (A); one dedicated 'TestBinaryStartup' that builds and execs the binary end-to-end as a single smoke check
options.rationale: Get the speed of in-process for the 6+ acceptance tests and one subprocess test that verifies the real binary path. Pays the build cost once instead of per-test.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: Expose display_id in SessionView (contract gap from research Finding 10)
items.context: Research Finding 10 states smoketest delegation works by 'call emulator API to create a headless session, receive DISPLAY value, pass it as an env var'. The current SessionView struct in api/livedesktop/types.go exposes scenario_name, state, vnc_port, ws_port, headless, app_running, and metrics — but NOT display_id. Without it, neither integration tests nor the future smoketest consumer can read the display (:0, :99, etc.) to use as DISPLAY env var. Session.View() has access to s.Display.DisplayID() but doesn't include it in the serialized view.

options.label: Add display_id field to SessionView in this item; populate in Session.View() from s.Display.DisplayID(); update existing unit tests to assert the field on creates
options.rationale: Small, localized API addition (~10 lines in types.go + service.go + test updates). Unblocks Phase 3 smoketest delegation and lets integration tests assert the real display value (e.g. matches '^:\d+$'). Aligns with the single source-of-truth principle: emulator knows the display, caller needs it.

options.label: Defer to a dedicated follow-up execute item; weaken Phase 1 tests to assert only indirect signals (headless=true, vnc_port=0, state=running)
options.rationale: Keeps this item's scope tight to test authoring. Downside: ships a known-incomplete contract for Phase 3 to trip over; a new item adds overhead and planning latency; integration tests have no way to verify the 'returned DISPLAY' claim from Finding 10.

options.label: Skip the DISPLAY assertion entirely; accept that smoketest delegation will address the contract when it needs it
options.rationale: Minimum effort now. Downside: violates research Finding 10 explicitly and leaves Phase 3 with no reference signal; 'just-in-time' contract evolution is an anti-pattern for a service API.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: app_path test fixture binary for launch_app assertions
items.context: Tests must launch a real application on the Xvfb display to verify the launch_app control action sets AppRunning=true and that procmetrics' xdotool-based window detector works. The binary must create an X window, run long enough for assertions (>5s), and be available on the target distros (Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 per d6). xclock ships with x11-apps; xterm is in most base installs; a custom Go fixture is heaviest but most self-contained.

options.label: xclock from x11-apps package — declare x11-apps as a test dependency and skip with clear message if not present
options.rationale: Trivially available (install in Dockerfile/CI base image), creates a visible X window for procmetrics window detection, runs indefinitely, has near-zero startup time. Standard choice for X11 integration tests across the Linux community.

options.label: xterm — invoked with '-e sleep 300' to keep it alive
options.rationale: More universally installed than xclock on some minimal images. Downside: xterm startup can be sluggish and its window name varies by theme, which may confuse xdotool-based window detection.

options.label: Custom Go fixture binary built from scenarios/vrooli-emulator/api/testdata/xfixture/ that opens an X11 window via go-x/xproto — checked in as source, built lazily by the test
options.rationale: Self-contained — no distro package dependency. Downside: adds Go dependencies, build complexity, and maintenance burden for something every Linux distro already provides via x11-apps.

options.label: Multiple candidates — try xclock first, fall back to xterm, fall back to xeyes; skip if none present
options.rationale: Maximum portability. Downside: test behavior diverges by host, making failures harder to reproduce.

items.context: Spec requires a CLI smoke test exercising 'session list/create/destroy/exec/logs'. The CLI lives at scenarios/vrooli-emulator/cli/, uses github.com/vrooli/cli-core/cliapp, and is invoked as 'vrooli-emulator' when installed. Memory rule feedback_cli_default_human_output.md requires default human output (no --json). Options differ on whether the test invokes the installed binary, builds and execs it, or imports the CLI packages in-process.

options.label: Build 'vrooli-emulator' binary to t.TempDir() via 'go build ./cli', exec it with os/exec against the in-process httptest.Server URL; assert on exit code + stdout substring matches
options.rationale: Exercises the real binary including flag parsing, installed-command framework, and output rendering. Build happens once per test run (shared helper), so cost is amortized. Matches operator reality most closely without paying ongoing binary-install cost.

options.label: 'go run ./cli ...' per command invocation against the httptest.Server URL
options.rationale: No explicit build step in test code. Downside: 'go run' compiles fresh each invocation (~2-3s each), which multiplies across 5+ subcommands, making the suite slow.

options.label: Import cli/domains/sessions and call runList/runCreate/runDestroy/runExec/runLogs in-process against the httptest.Server URL; capture stdout via pipe
options.rationale: Fastest. Downside: skips the cliapp framework, flag parsing, and binary-packaging path — which is exactly what a 'smoke test' is supposed to catch. Reduces to a library test.

options.label: Use the installed 'vrooli-emulator' command (assume pre-installed on CI via scenario setup)
options.rationale: Tests the actual user-facing binary. Downside: requires setup machinery to install before tests run and couples test runs to the installation pipeline being green.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.context: The absorbed scope from retired execute/vrooli-emulator-linux-first requires 'at minimum Ubuntu LTS 22.04 and 24.04'. The dev host runs one specific kernel/distro; other distros must be validated somehow. Options trade setup cost against signal strength: CI matrix runs on every commit but costs cycles; documented targets relies on operator discipline; containerized validation is hermetic but heavy.

options.label: Document in scenarios/vrooli-emulator/docs/runbook.md that 22.04 and 24.04 are the supported matrix; verify once manually during this item; leave CI on the existing default runner
options.rationale: Minimum cost, fastest to close. Leverages the sibling chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation which already absorbs runbook content. Appropriate for a Phase 1 item where test authoring is the primary deliverable and the matrix is a support statement, not a per-commit gate.

options.label: Add a GitHub Actions matrix job ({os: [ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04]}) that runs the integration suite on both runners per commit touching scenarios/vrooli-emulator/**
options.rationale: Strongest signal — every change is validated on both distros. Downside: doubles CI minutes for the scenario; adds workflow maintenance; requires confirmation that GitHub-provided 22.04 and 24.04 runners have Xvfb/x11vnc/websockify available or installable. acceptance_allow for this item is scenarios/vrooli-emulator/** which does not cover .github/workflows — this option would require an acceptance_allow expansion.

options.label: Add a 'make test-distros' target that runs the integration suite inside ubuntu:22.04 and ubuntu:24.04 containers (docker run with Xvfb inside) — invoked manually on demand or pre-release
options.rationale: Hermetic and reproducible locally; no CI matrix cost. Downside: adds ~2-3 minutes per distro for container pull + test run; requires Docker on the validator's machine; runs less often than CI so regressions land later.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.text: Host precondition verification: the current dev host has Xvfb, xvfb-run, x11vnc, websockify, and xdotool at /usr/bin/. No additional installation is needed to run real-backend integration tests locally. xclock (for d4 option A) requires 'apt install x11-apps' if not present. Tests will include a pre-flight check that skips with a clear message when any required binary is missing, matching the precedent in scenarios/vrooli-emulator/api/screenrecording/display_test.go:63.

Gap vs research Finding 10: the current SessionView does not expose display_id (confirmed via grep of api/livedesktop/types.go:105-135). Finding 10 explicitly states smoketest delegation reads the returned DISPLAY value. d3 above resolves whether to fix this in scope or defer — not resolving it means Phase 3 (execute/smoketest-delegate-display-to-emulator) will either duplicate this decision or ship with a contract workaround. Recommended path: d3=A adds ~10 lines and unblocks downstream work cleanly.

plan_updates: Round 1 scaffold: created plan.md with all 13 mandatory sections populated. Sections filled from existing research and scenario code: Purpose, Required Reading (with kind-required skills + discovered test/cross-platform-readiness + plan-authoring required reading), Problem Statement (with d3 contract gap surfaced), Scope (in/out with acceptance_allow honored), Current Technical Context (listing every relevant file and the verified host X11 deps), Target End State (6 assertions + harness + CLI smoke + matrix + testing.json wiring), Implementation Strategy (5 phases A-E gated by d1-d6), Contract Decisions (Settled + Open + Prohibited), Testing Plan (8 verification gates), Rollout/Validation Checklist, Risks + Mitigations (10 rows), Scenario Restart Note (conditional on d3), Non-goals, Definition of Done (12 items). Every open question points at the corresponding workshop decision; no hidden assumptions.
